title: A decomposition splits a record into parts: read what each part is for and what it cannot say
summary: POD splits a stack of video frames into spatial patterns ranked by energy. DMD splits it into patterns that each have one frequency and one growth rate. EMD and the Hilbert-Huang spectrum split a single time series into oscillations whose frequency may drift. Each method answers a different question, and each has a known way to mislead.

media.alt: Three images of a flame side by side, title MVI_8036 windowed full-frame POD/DMD, 8 s window, 192 frames. Left: mean field, a bright vertical flame in a magma colour map. Middle: POD mode 0 (42 percent energy), a blue and red pair of tilted lobes along the flame axis. Right: DMD mode 0 (0.00 Hz), a blue flame-shaped region inside a red surround.

source.caption: Windowed POD/DMD modes
source.note: Two decompositions of the same MVI_8036 record. Figure 09 takes an 8 s window of 192 full video frames and shows the mean field, the leading POD (proper orthogonal decomposition) mode with its energy share and the leading DMD (dynamic mode decomposition) mode with its frequency. Figure 10 decomposes the height time series by empirical mode decomposition into six intrinsic mode functions and shows the Hilbert-Huang spectrum.

read_the_figure.question: Which spatial patterns carry most of the variation in a short window of flame video, and at what frequencies do they oscillate?
read_the_figure.axes: Figure 09 has no numeric axes: each panel is the same image area (height up, flame axis vertical), coloured by value. Figure 10, top: x is time (s after ignition, about 300 to 535 s), y is the amplitude of each of six intrinsic mode functions, stacked with offsets. Figure 10, bottom: x is time, y is instantaneous frequency in Hz (about -12 to 12), colour is amplitude.
look_at: Mean field (09, left): the time-averaged brightness. Everything else is a departure from this.

POD mode 0 (09, middle): the pattern, with its energy share in the title (42 percent). Positive and negative lobes of opposite colour mean 'when one is brighter the other is darker'. A tilted pair along the axis is the signature of the flame bending sideways.
DMD mode 0 (09, right): the pattern that shares one frequency. The title says 0.00 Hz, which is a non-oscillating mode.
IMFs (10, top): six curves from the fastest oscillation (bottom, thick black band) to the slowest trend (top). They add up to the original series.

Hilbert-Huang spectrum (10, bottom): each dot is one instantaneous frequency at one time. A horizontal band is a steady oscillation; a band that wanders is a drifting one. Points near plus and minus 12 Hz and below zero are not trustworthy.
read_the_figure.proves: If the leading POD mode looks like a physically sensible motion (here a sideways bending) and carries a large energy share, then most of the variation in that window is one coherent motion. If the Hilbert-Huang bands are narrow and continuous, the oscillation is nearly periodic.
if_wrong: A leading POD mode that looks like the mean field: the window is dominated by the mean or by an overall brightness change, not by motion.
A DMD mode at 0 Hz: it is the steady component; a flicker mode would show up at a nonzero frequency.
Negative frequencies or dots pinned at the edges of the spectrum: the Hilbert transform is misbehaving on a mode that is not a clean narrow-band oscillation, or the signal is at the Nyquist limit.
IMFs that do not separate scales (similar frequency in two of them): mode mixing, a known weakness of EMD.
must_check: The window length and frame count (here 8 s and 192 frames, so 24 frames per second, a Nyquist frequency of 12 Hz).
Whether the mean is subtracted before POD. Here a separate mean field is shown, which suggests so.
The energy of each mode, not only the first.
What each IMF colour is in the spectrum: the figure does not say.
Units of the IMF amplitude: the axis is labelled 'IMFs (offset)' without a unit.
as_drawn: Values read off by eye or from the panel titles.
09: window 8 s, 192 frames; POD mode 0 carries 42 percent of the energy; DMD mode 0 is at 0.00 Hz.
10, IMFs: six curves, the slowest rising to about 7700 offset units over about 40 s and then staying roughly flat; the fastest is a noisy band of amplitude of order 100 to 300 units about zero.

10, spectrum: three dense coloured bands, near 0 to 1 Hz (green), about 1 to 3 Hz (orange) and a broad cloud from about 1 to 6 Hz (blue), plus scattered points near plus and minus 12 Hz and a few between -10 and 0 Hz.

terms.meaning: Each video frame, with its pixels flattened into one column; the matrix has one column per frame.
Proper orthogonal decomposition: the singular vectors of the snapshot matrix, ranked by how much variance they carry.
The squared singular value divided by the sum of all squared singular values.
Dynamic mode decomposition: spatial modes each with one frequency and one growth or decay rate, from the best-fit linear map between consecutive frames.
The factor by which a mode is multiplied each frame. Its angle gives the frequency, its size the growth.
Empirical mode decomposition splits a series into intrinsic mode functions (IMFs), each an oscillation about zero whose amplitude and frequency may vary slowly.
The instantaneous frequency and amplitude of each IMF, plotted against time.
Half the frame rate; the highest frequency a sampled record can represent.

remember: POD ranks patterns by energy but does not give frequencies; DMD gives frequencies but not a ranking by energy.
POD is the singular value decomposition of the frame stack with the mean removed.
A DMD eigenvalue with angle zero is a steady mode (0 Hz).
A window of length T resolves frequency steps of 1/T, and the frame rate sets the ceiling at half of it.
EMD is adaptive and not a transform with a unique inverse theory, so check each result by reconstruction.

understand.title: Why POD and DMD are both shown
understand.text: POD answers 'which pattern explains most of the variation', DMD answers 'which pattern oscillates at one frequency'. Seeing them side by side shows that the dominant pattern and the dominant oscillation need not be the same thing.

understand.title: Reading the POD pair
understand.text: A tilted red and blue lobe pair along the flame axis says that, in this window, the main variation is the flame bending from one side to the other, with the tip side and the base side moving oppositely.

understand.title: What the 0.00 Hz DMD mode is
understand.text: A mode at 0 Hz and with eigenvalue near one is the persistent part of the flame: the structure that does not change over the window. It is not a flicker mode, so the flicker modes would be the other DMD modes, which this figure does not show.

understand.title: Why a second method for the height series
understand.text: Flicker onset is not stationary: its frequency and amplitude drift. A Fourier spectrum smears such a signal over a band. EMD adapts to the local oscillation, and the Hilbert-Huang spectrum shows how the dominant frequency moves in time. Its weakness is that the instantaneous frequency is only meaningful for narrow-band modes.

steps.title: Stack the frames
steps.tex: X=[\,x_1\ x_2\ \cdots\ x_N\,]\in\mathbb R^{m\times N},\qquad x_k=\operatorname{vec}\!\left(I_k-\bar I\right)
steps.note: Each frame is flattened to a vector with the mean image subtracted. Here N = 192 frames over 8 s, so the sampling interval is 1/24 s.

steps.title: POD as an SVD
steps.note: The columns of U are the spatial POD modes, ranked by singular value. The energy share E_k is what the figure prints for mode 0 (42 percent).

steps.title: Best-fit linear map between frames
steps.note: DMD finds the matrix that best advances one frame to the next; the superscript plus is the pseudo-inverse. In practice it is computed in the low-dimensional POD basis.

steps.title: Eigenvalues give frequency and growth
steps.note: The angle of the eigenvalue sets the frequency; its modulus sets whether a mode grows (above one) or decays (below one). lambda equal to one is a steady mode at 0 Hz.

steps.title: Window limits
steps.note: An 8 s window cannot distinguish frequencies closer than 0.125 Hz, and with 24 frames per second nothing above 12 Hz can be represented.

steps.title: Instantaneous frequency of an IMF
steps.note: The Hilbert transform builds the analytic signal of one IMF c(t); its phase derivative is the instantaneous frequency. The estimate is meaningful only if the IMF is narrow-band; a noisy or mixed IMF gives negative or erratic frequencies.

worked.title: Frequency and growth of a DMD eigenvalue, illustrative
worked.problem: With 24 frames per second, a DMD eigenvalue is lambda = 0.99 e^{0.5 i}. What are its frequency and growth rate? What would lambda = 1 mean?
worked.answer: About 1.9 Hz and slowly decaying (-0.24 per second). An eigenvalue exactly equal to 1 has angle 0 and modulus 1, so it is a steady, non-decaying mode at 0.00 Hz, like the DMD mode shown in the figure. The eigenvalue here is illustrative; the figure does not print its eigenvalues.

analyze.q: POD mode 0 carries 42 percent of the energy. What does that leave unexplained, and how would you decide how many modes to keep?
analyze.hint: Cumulative energy and a gap in the singular values.

analyze.q: The DMD mode shown has frequency 0.00 Hz. What can you conclude about flicker from this panel alone, and what would you look at next?
analyze.hint: The other DMD eigenvalues and their frequencies.

analyze.q: The Hilbert-Huang spectrum has dots at about plus and minus 12 Hz and some below zero. Give two reasons these should not be read as flame frequencies.

evaluate.q: Is it fair to describe the figure 09 panels as 'coherent structures recovered from video'? What would make the claim firmer?
evaluate.hint: Mode energies, repeated windows, and a frequency peak.

evaluate.q: For a non-stationary height series, compare a Fourier spectrum with the Hilbert-Huang spectrum: which would you trust for the onset and why?

create: Design a version of figure 09 that shows the first four POD modes with their energy shares and the first four oscillating DMD modes with their frequencies and growth rates.
Redraw the Hilbert-Huang spectrum with each IMF labelled, points beyond the Nyquist limit masked, and the Fourier spectrum of the same series alongside.

checks.q: What is the difference between a POD mode and a DMD mode?
checks.answer: A POD mode is a spatial pattern ranked by how much of the variance it carries; a DMD mode is a pattern with a single frequency and a single growth rate, found from a linear model of how frames evolve.

checks.q: 192 frames span 8 s. What is the frame rate and the Nyquist frequency?
checks.answer: 192 divided by 8 is 24 frames per second, so the Nyquist frequency is 12 Hz.

checks.q: A DMD mode has eigenvalue exactly 1. What does it represent?
checks.answer: A steady mode: angle zero means 0 Hz and modulus one means it neither grows nor decays. It is the persistent part of the flame, not an oscillation.

checks.q: Is a negative instantaneous frequency in a Hilbert-Huang spectrum a real physical frequency?
checks.answer: Not usually. It signals that the phase of the analytic signal ran backwards, typically because the IMF is not a clean narrow-band oscillation or contains riding waves. Treat such points as artefacts.

checks.q: How would you check an EMD result?
checks.answer: Add the IMFs and compare with the original series, repeat with a small amount of added noise to see whether the IMFs change (mode mixing), and compare the dominant frequencies with an ordinary spectrum.

provenance.notes: Standard theory only. Read-off values approximate. Concerns for the owner: (1) the DMD mode shown is labelled 0.00 Hz, i.e. the steady/mean-like mode, not an oscillating flicker mode, so the caption's 'coherent structures' fits the POD panel better than the DMD one; (2) the Hilbert-Huang spectrum shows negative instantaneous frequencies and dense points pinned at about plus and minus 12 Hz (the Nyquist limit for the 24 frames per second implied by 192 frames in 8 s), which look like estimation artefacts; (3) the IMF panel has a y axis in offset units with no physical unit. The figures do not label which IMF colour is which in the spectrum.
